chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Burayd al-Ijli who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): … he said: … and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not place in the religion any discomfort; for 'difficulty' is more extreme than 'discomfort'.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between difficulty and discomfort in Islamic religion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential principle of *al-yusr* (ease) by distinguishing between *dhīq* (discomfort or mild difficulty) and *haraj* (severe hardship), asserting that Allah did not impose the latter in the religion. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly understanding that religious obligations are calibrated to human capacity, avoiding excessive burden. It serves as a foundational text for deriving general legal maxims regarding the removal of difficulty (*raf' al-haraj*) in Islamic law.

en.ammaar-muslim: 9. [9/-] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Burayd al-Ijli who said:
I said to Abi Ja’far عليه السلام: … he said: … and Allāh Blessed and Exalted did not place in the religion any discomfort for “difficulty” is more extreme than “discomfort”.
